question: A square pyramid has lateral surface area equal to twice the base area. If base side = 6 cm, find slant height.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

For a square pyramid, Lateral Surface Area (LSA) = 2 × base side × slant height = 2al

Base Area = a²

Given LSA = 2 × Base Area

⇒ 2al = 2a² ⇒ l = a

Since the base side (a) is 6 cm, the slant height (l) is also 6 cm.

**∴ The correct answer is 6 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Base side (a) = 6 cm

Lateral Surface Area = 2 × Base Area

**Formula Used:**

Area of square base = a²

Lateral Surface Area of square pyramid = 4 × (1/2 × base × slant height) = 2 × a × l

 

 
• 
 

 

 
• 
 
• 
 
• 
 
 Base side (a) = 6 cm
 Slant height (l)
 Height (h)
 Square Pyramid

**Calculations:**

⇒ Base Area = 6² = 36 cm²

⇒ Lateral Surface Area = 2 × 36 = 72 cm²

⇒ 2 × a × l = 72

⇒ 2 × 6 × l = 72

⇒ 12l = 72

⇒ l = 72 ÷ 12 = 6 cm

**∴ The correct answer is 6 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Total Surface Area (TSA)

The TSA of a square pyramid is the sum of its base area and lateral surface area. Formula: TSA = a² + 2al

Volume of Square Pyramid

The volume is one-third of the product of the base area and the vertical height. Formula: V = (1/3) × a² × h

Relation between Heights

Using the Pythagorean theorem inside the pyramid, the slant height (l), vertical height (h), and base side (a) form a right-angled triangle: l² = h² + (a/2)²
